page: Microsoft Azure DC1s_v3 is a single-core virtual machine from the DCSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The server is configured with 1 physical core, 1 thread, and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core capabilities but overall constrained multi-core and memory performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scored 1875.88, and the Geekbench single-core score reached 1628.0. However, due to the single-core limitation, the multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores are also low, at 1875.88 and 1640.0 respectively. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only large block speeds at 13.2 GB/sec and write speeds at 10.83 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform at average levels, with gzip compression single-threaded at 28.27 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.48 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the DC1s_v3 is its single-core architecture, which limits parallel processing, database operations, and web serving throughput. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides a dedicated Intel Xeon core and a relatively high memory-to-core ratio of 1:8 without the overhead of larger multi-core instances. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic cryptography tasks, small-scale text processing, or low-demand utility services that require dedicated CPU allocation and a small memory footprint.
